chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who marries without a proof (witnesses), he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.بَيِّنَةٍ: Proof or evidence, specifically referring to witnesses in the context of marriage contracts
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible (a common legal phrase indicating validity)
key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجُ: He marries (verb form indicating the action of contracting marriage)

ai.seo_question: Is a marriage valid in Shia Islam if it is performed without witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the absence of witnesses (bayyinah) does not invalidate the marriage contract, reflecting the Shia view that while witnesses are recommended for public recognition, they are not a strict condition for the core validity (sihha) of the union. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital formalities, distinguishing between the essential elements of consent and the evidentiary requirements for public proof.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who married without a proof. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “About the case of a man who marries without witness, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
